subject: ArborPay: sudden reserved throughput degradation, error-rate spike
messages:
From: Alex Chen <ops@arborpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@arborpay.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 14:27:00 -0400
Subject: Production alerts — throughput down, 500s increasing

Jordan —

We started seeing customer-facing errors around 13:40 EDT. Key symptoms:
- 3x median token-latency for generate requests (spiked from ~120ms to ~380ms)
- error-rate (5xx) on RL generation route up to ~6% for the last 30m
- observed throttling / queueing in our reserved capacity pool; some requests get queued for >5s

We are on Reserved plan DE-ARBR-01 and pinned to rwinf/redwood:gptx-64b-v2. This is impacting checkout personalization flows. Can you confirm whether this is a customer-side configuration or something in the dedicated pool? We captured a few stack traces and a SAN screenshot (attached).

We need an immediate triage call and an ETA for a mitigation path — ArborPay SRE team is standing by.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Senior SRE, ArborPay
attachments: arborpay-error-snapshot-20280403.png
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <ops@arborpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 14:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Production alerts — throughput down, 500s increasing

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot.

Immediate steps:
- I've alerted Eng (Marissa) and our Capacity team (Neha).
- Can you confirm whether ArborPay is using the token-cache override we discussed last quarter? If so, please call that out — it changes request sizes and batching behavior.
- I'll stand up a 30m bridge now and loop in Engineering + Capacity owners. Proposed bridge: in 10 minutes (14:52 EDT).

Short-term mitigation options we'll evaluate on the bridge:
- Temporarily shift your traffic to an alternate compatible model variant (lower memory / higher concurrency) to relieve the pool.
- Bump reserved concurrency for the pool (if headroom exists) and apply temporary prioritization for ArborPay routes.
- Forced prefix-KV cache invalidation if there's observed KV blowup.

I attached the link to our incident workspace; please upload any additional logs you have.

Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
(bridge: https://meet.redwoodinference.com/j/jordan-arborpay-0428)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <ops@arborpay.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 15:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Production alerts — throughput down, 500s increasing

Joined the bridge. Quick diagnostics from the reserved pool telemetry (attached CSV):
- GPU utilization per node in ArborPay pool is at 92%-97% on average for the last 45m.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 84% to 51% around 13:22 — suggests working set growth.
- Small cohort of requests show rapid increases in sequence length per request (some up to +3x).
- We observed transient OOM retries on 2 warm nodes causing request retries and a cascading queue.

Immediate mitigation in progress (actions taken):
- Scale: spun a one-time +12% elasticity to the pool (non-committed burst) — metrics are starting to show lower queue depth but uncertain on sustained effect.
- Routing: enabling fallback routing to a compatible-but-smaller quantized variant for non-critical routes (applied to 20% of traffic).
- Cache: backfilling prefix cache warmers for the top endpoints; running an eviction pass.

As next steps we recommend:
1) For tonight: keep fallback in place and increase burst to +25% if queue depth climbs again.
2) For 72h: we need to provision additional reserved nodes (or convert some burst capacity into committed) and run a root-cause on working-set growth (prompt changes / new features).

Attachments: reserved-pool-metrics-2028Q1.csv

Marissa Cole
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <ops@arborpay.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@arborpay.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: ArborPay — exec escalation & next 24h ask

Jordan / Marissa —

Status readout appreciated. This has crossed the threshold for exec attention given customer impact and revenue sensitivity. Two asks:
1) We need a concise remediation timeline with owner + ETA for each item below within 2 hours: capacity (nodes committed), routing fallback %, and customer-facing error reduction target.
2) Confirm compensation/credits exposure if this persists >24h and a point estimate of impact to ArborPay SLA. Finance may be engaged.

Marissa — prioritize a reproducible test case that explains the working-set expansion (prompt pattern or user change) and whether quantization or kernel selection triggered OOMs. If you need an emergency allocation from infra, escalate now.

Jordan — keep ArborPay leadership updated; let's schedule a 09:30am check tomorrow if needed.

Marcus Lin
VP, Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference
From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@arborpay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Chen <ops@arborpay.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Apr 2028 16:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: ArborPay — exec escalation & next 24h ask

Marcus / Jordan —

Appreciate the rapid engagement. ArborPay is willing to take the temporary fallback routing while you stabilize. Two asks from our side:
- Daily 30-minute sync for the next three days (stand-up at 10:00 EDT) to get progress updates and confirm no regression in personalization quality.
- If you expect credits or SLA remediation, please share the proposed calculation as soon as possible so we can share with procurement.

We will also send a small dataset (anonymized) that shows the longer-than-usual sequences that spiked earlier.

Thanks,
Priya Rao
Head of Product Operations, ArborPay
